references.text: Lot saw that the whole Jordan Valley was well-watered - this is the background for his choice in verse 11.
Describes the consequence of Lot's choice: he settled among the cities of the valley and moved his tents toward Sodom, whose inhabitants were very wicked.
Lot traveled with Abram from Ur of the Chaldeans, providing the background for their shared journey and later separation.
Tells of Lot's fate in Sodom and the destruction of the cities of the valley, a direct result of his choice of the Jordan Valley.
Esau and Jacob also had to separate because their possessions were too great for them to live together - a parallel to Abram and Lot's separation.
Describes how the wealth of Abram and Lot led to strife between their herdsmen, which is why they had to part ways.
